RESULT — Logistic regression of remission on Age, BMI, Gender (n = 80).

PRIMARY ANSWER: The change in log-odds of remission for each one-year increase in patient age is −0.080 (exact estimate −0.0795; 95% CI −0.131 to −0.028; p = 0.0025; OR = 0.92 per year). That is, each additional year of age is associated with an approximately 0.08 decrease in the log-odds of remission (about an 8% reduction in the odds of remission per year), holding BMI and gender constant.

FULL COEFFICIENT TABLE (primary model, remission = PR [1] vs SD/PD [0]; n = 80, converged MLE):
                 coef      OR    95% CI (OR)        p
  const       0.9181   2.5045   0.011 – 592.16   0.742
  Age        −0.0795   0.9236   0.877 – 0.972    0.0025
  BMI         0.1621   1.1760   0.950 – 1.456    0.136
  female(=1)  0.6132   1.8463   0.632 – 5.395    0.262
(Age 95% CI on the log-odds scale: −0.1311 to −0.0280.)

Diagnostics: model converged (max-iteration checks passed); no separation — fitted probabilities span 0.120–0.903, all parameters finite; log-likelihood −48.58 on 80 observations. Predictors were complete for all 80 substantive rows, so no cases were dropped or imputed.

Sensitivity analysis (pre-declared alternative outcome coding, remission = PR+SD [1] vs PD [0]): Age coefficient −0.0605 per year (95% CI −0.1161 to −0.0050; p = 0.0327; OR = 0.94). The direction and magnitude are consistent with the primary model; the difference between codings is only 0.019 log-odds units. Under both definitions, older age is significantly associated with lower log-odds of remission.

Data handling recap: 41 padding rows in Sheet1 (rows 80–120, including one row containing only a whitespace Age cell) were dropped; Age was cast to numeric (lossless for all 80 patients); Gender coded Female = 1, Male = 0; unpenalized statsmodels Logit MLE.
